nodes.label: Business Dashboard (/console)
nodes.rationale: Total Transactions is the headline because an EPS partner is billed per API call; Eloka leads with GTV because its users move other people's money for commission — the inverse business.

nodes.label: One requestPayload key per call
nodes.rationale: A multi-key payload had upstream silently omit two datasets — two blank widgets on a healthy account with no error anywhere. The four calls run concurrently so wall-clock is the slowest, not the sum.

nodes.label: pickDataset (exact-before-normalized key matching)
nodes.rationale: Upstream naming is inconsistent (three of four datasets snake-to-camel, one does not), so exact candidates are tried before normalized ones and an ambiguous normalized match resolves to nothing rather than to whichever key serialized first.

nodes.label: buildDashboardView (upstream normalizer)
nodes.rationale: Downline-only widgets are dropped at the backend boundary so they never reach the browser; any block may arrive JSON-encoded so everything goes through one decode, and a service map arriving as an array is rejected rather than rendering 'Service 0' nonsense.

nodes.label: Server-side IST date-window maths
nodes.rationale: The backend runs UTC but Eko's data is stamped IST, so computing 'today' in UTC would open a Delhi partner's window 5h30m late; the browser sends only a preset because an arbitrary window is an unbounded upstream scan.

nodes.label: Dashboard caching (scoped keys, closed-window TTL)
nodes.rationale: Windows other than today end at yesterday 23:59:59 — closed windows whose numbers cannot change — so they hold 900s. The scope hash prevents a shared Redis from serving UAT numbers to a live partner, and an empty service list is never cached.

nodes.label: Zero versus absent (shape logging)
nodes.rationale: A quiet week and an out-of-scope account both look like zeros, so zeros are never hidden and the route logs raw= (what each dry call actually received) — without it an upstream answering under an unasked-for name would be invisible. shapeOf reports keys and kinds only, never a partner's values.

nodes.label: Service filter (narrowed 1044 master list)
nodes.rationale: Options are recomputed only from an unfiltered view, or a filtered response would collapse the dropdown to the current selection; it resets on window change and is a native <select> rather than 150 lines of Radix that does not exist yet.

nodes.label: Most Used Services falls back to Success Rates
nodes.rationale: An approximation, not a second source of truth: if upstream ever scopes the two blocks differently the counts drift. Delete it once mostUsedServices is reliable.

nodes.label: React.lazy recharts widgets
nodes.rationale: AppServer imports ConsoleHome eagerly for the static build, so a plain import would drag ~250KB of charting into the SSG bundle; each chart also renders a text summary because an SVG is invisible to a screen reader and jsdom measures zero.

nodes.label: Dashboard degradation ladder (501/401/502)
nodes.rationale: Mounted unconditionally and answering a named 501 lets the console say 'not on this deployment' instead of guessing at a 404; a failing 1044 is non-fatal because refusing the filter would turn a cosmetic outage into a broken one.
